entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.
Heard counsel for the applicant and Sri Vinod Kumar Tiwari, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application, under Section 439 Cr.P.C., has been filed with a prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 78 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 504 & 506 I.P.C.,
Police Station- Izzatnagar, District- Bareilly during pendency of the trial.
3. Counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
The applicant was neither the vendor, vendee nor the marginal witness of the alleged sale deed.
No amount has been credited in the account of the applicant.
The applicant is not a beneficiary of the illicit transaction.
The applicant has no concern with the alleged sale deed nor the applicant is a member of any gang.

The criminal history of the applicant has been explained in para Rajeev Kishore vs State Of U.P. on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39931240/
1 no. 13 of the bail application.

entities.text: para Rajeev Kishore vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 11.06.2023.

In case he is enlarged on bail,
he will not misuse the said liberty.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid facts from the record.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record this Court prima facie finds that the applicant was neither the vendor, vendee nor the marginal witness of the sale deed.
At present, there is no substantive evidence against the applicant.

Further, the applicant has remained confined for more than five months and after submission of the charge-sheet there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

6. Let the applicant, Rajeev Kishore involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned on the following conditions that:
i. the applicant shall not temper with the prosecution evidence; ii. the applicant shall not pressurize the prosecution witness; and, iii. the applicant shall appear on each and every date fixed by the trial court.
7.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 16.11.2023 Sachin Mishra  Rajeev Kishore vs State Of U.P. on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39931240/
